fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they rely purely on substantial equivalency (often with automatic practice privileges), combine it with an experience-based fallback path, require exam passage plus character/CPE without explicit equivalency language, demand reciprocal treatment from the other state, or address only partial exam credit.

Holder of a valid CPA certificate from another state; examination may be waived; must meet moral character and citizenship requirements

Applicant must have certificate, registration or license from another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements, or meet specific education and experience requirements

Applicant must hold a current, active, unrestricted CPA license from another state with standards substantially equivalent to California's education, examination, and experience requirements; must not have committed acts constituting grounds for denial under Section 480.

Applicant must be duly licensed, certified, or registered in good standing in another state or territory with substantially equivalent experience or credentials, or hold a current and valid license for at least one year with substantially similar scope of practice
